General Summary: The National Black-footed Ferret Conservation Center (the Center) in Carr, Colorado houses approximately 66% of the world’s ex-situ population of endangered black-footed ferrets (Mustela nigripes). The Center’s mission is to maintain a viable assurance population of black-footed ferrets in managed care and to produce healthy kits to support reintroduction efforts to the wild. Black- footed ferrets are reintroduced to select sites in several states each year in an effort to meet recovery goals. The Center houses at least 170-185 breeding ferrets year-round. This number doubles during summer and fall of each year as hundreds of kits are born and more are transferred to the Center from five zoo breeding facilities for veterinary processing and behavioral preconditioning. The Center needs a local veterinary diagnostic laboratory to use for testing samples of sick or dead ferrets to look

certifications_partner.text: The loss of the Platform Lift Assembly catastrophically degrades the vessel's multi-mission execution capabilities, a core design attribute of the Independence-class (Independence-variant) Littoral Combat Ship platform. The ship's ability to rapidly load, stow, and deploy mission packages, transit ordnance to the flight deck or mission bay, and conduct sustained aviation or surface warfare operations would be severely impeded. This degradation places the ship well below its minimum operational "redlines" for cargo handling and combat systems readiness. Operating in such a compromised state, particularly during underway exercises and certification events, would violate established safety protocols and introduce an unacceptable level of risk to personnel working on or near the lift. Furthermore, the mechanical instability of the lift platform presents a significant secondary hazard, creating a dangerous crush and fall environment for crew members, which mandates immediate corrective action.
